findings.claim: In html-css-js-final-mcq-30, the third distractor says 'Working... forever, because the loop stops the last line from running' (line 253), but the stem shows no loop: it calls 'buildReport(rows); // synchronous, about 3 seconds' (line 248). A careful reader has to guess what 'the loop' means. The stem also says the work ends after about 3 seconds, so the distractor is answered by the stem rather than by event-loop knowledge, and only two distractors remain plausible.
findings.recommendation: Change the distractor to a misconception that fits the code shown. For example: 'Working... until buildReport returns, then Done, because the browser paints between statements in a handler'. Or: 'Only Working..., because the second assignment is skipped while the page is frozen'. Each feedback should then point to the render-after-task rule.

items.note: Resolved. html-css-js-final-mcq-02 (line 14) keys footer for a byline and contact line that close an article. The semantic page practises footer only at page level: Activity 2's news page maps 'F Copyright and contact' to footer, and the Activity 3 recipe markup maps 'div class legal, holding the copyright line' to footer ('the copyright line closes the page'). No semantic quiz, mastery or Course Review item poses a footer that closes a section or article, and the mastery check names footer only as a wrong option for a side box. Item 02 applies the taught definition ('closing information for the page or its section') at a level the learner has not practised, with aside, section and header as real alternatives. The step up is small, but it fits a band-1 opener at position 2.

Resolved. The re-asked error-handling item 30 has been replaced. html-css-js-final-mcq-30 (line 246) is now an event-loop rendering prediction: status text is set, a 3-second synchronous function runs, then 'Done' is set. The page teaches 'run a task to completion, then drain all microtasks, then let the browser render' and 'nothing paints until it ends', and the quiz '::o2 why it freezes::' asks the abstract reason. No practice item asks what a user sees from DOM writes during a long task, so this is an applied step up; I searched for 'Working...' and 'never painted' and found nothing. handling-http-errors-and-problemdetail-responses is still keyed by items 11 and 25 (line 199), and items 25 and 30 no longer share a decision. As a band-2 or band-3 item it is a fitting close. It shares its core idea, 'long synchronous work holds the one thread until it ends', with item 22, but item 22 keys the await-yields-only-while-pending distinction and item 30 keys painting, so the two are different decisions.

Resolved. html-css-js-final-mcq-25 (line 201) now sends headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, so the 400 in the stem no longer conflicts with the calling-your-spring-boot-api page's teaching that a header-less POST gets 415.
